top.line: Local and niche publishers own trust: take in commodity, certify big outlets upwards for pay, and maintain stories.
top.para: Value lies with publishers close to readers in language, culture and expertise. They can serve commodity facts and global news from their readers' viewpoint, and certify big outlets' local stories for payment. That needs open, billable interfaces like UK open banking, a map of who reports versus recycles, and paid maintenance of stories, as with software maintainers.

in-short.line: Eight lines: local value, trust, commodity in, certification up, shadows, open interfaces, recycling map, maintenance.
in-short.para: The local and niche hold the value and the trust. Commodity flows in and is served from the reader's view. Certification flows up and is paid. Unsourced stories are shadows. Interfaces should open, as UK banks' did. Who reports and who recycles should be mapped, cuts made visible. Stories need maintaining like software.

value.line: Focused local, regional or expert publishers hold the trust, and trust is where value now lies.
value.para: Alongside large generic organisations, more focused publishers will emerge, and that is where charging and investing in journalism make sense. Close to readers' language, culture and region, their business models stay aligned with readers, while bigger organisations drift toward rent extraction and lose edge and trust.

commodity.line: Local sites should carry commodity facts and global news, agent-captured, sourced, and told from readers' viewpoint.
commodity.para: Weather, sport results, trains and markets come from official sources and can be kept current by agents at little cost. Global news belongs there too, explained for local readers in their language. This keeps the habit of returning that Kok warns not to lose, without consuming newsroom time.

open.line: Commodity must flow through open interfaces; UK open banking, ordered by the CMA, is the precedent.
open.para: The CMA found in 2016 that banks lacked competition and recommended open banking; since 2018 customers share account data securely through a standard built under its order, and Open Banking Limited reports over 18 million active users. News lacks this: of 913 watched pages, 59 bot-challenged and 15 paywalled. Standard, billable access would serve all.

certify.line: Big outlets' local stories should cite and pay a trusted local source that certifies them.
certify.para: Reading about my town on a big site, I would expect a trusted local outlet or agency employing local journalists as the source, certifying the story or adding a caveat. The big outlet pays per use. A story with no such source is a shadow, and readers can go to the local original instead.

recycles.line: Map who reports and who recycles; recycling should be paid for, and cutting experts should be visible.
recycles.para: The PHP site's captures show who reported first, who quoted whom and who rewrote later. Global outlets reusing others' work should send reporters or pay. Correspondent cuts stay hidden today; losing a cybersecurity correspondent or a subject expert should show on the site and in its trust, because nobody then certifies or maintains those stories.

maintain.line: A newsroom's history is like case law, and stories with changing facts go off like milk.
maintain.para: Stories are referenced and built on, but revised numbers, withdrawn claims and rewritten sources make them stale. An expert must keep each story true or mark it no longer current, which is ongoing, paid work.

software.line: The same as software maintainers: whoever does the expert work should be paid and sign off.
software.para: Maintainers should be paid and sign the versions we run; journalists and experts should be paid and sign the stories built on their work. Free-riders are invisible in both, and harm appears only when the expert leaves. Making who signs for what visible is how both get funded.

exists.line: Capture, provenance, story graphs and signed notes exist; paid certification, open billable interfaces and recycling maps are proposals.
exists.para: Existing: the PHP site's capture, provenance and source watch, stories kept as graphs including the simulated bridge story, and signed notes and keys on pki.sgit.ai. Proposed: per-use paid certification, open billable news interfaces, a public map of reporting versus recycling, and trust reflecting staffing.

limits.line: A model, not a market; local trust argued, not measured; open banking is a mechanism parallel; many big outlets still report.
limits.para: No local publisher is paid for certification today. Trust in local news is argued here rather than measured. The open-banking comparison concerns opening interfaces by order, not regulating news identically. Many large outlets still send reporters; the aim is to make the difference visible.

sources.line: My memo replying to Kok, Open Banking Limited's account, the PHP site's source watch, related articles.
sources.para: My voice memo of 25 October 2026 replying to Bert Kok's essay; Open Banking Limited's page on its origins, read on 25 October; the PHP story site's source watch and evidence at v0.21.6; and related newsroom articles on owning the stack and trust, signing, shadows, maintainers, accountability, php2shell's side stories and the bridge story.
